about: Urizen's talking head on Qián (1), line 6. Urizen, Blake's measurer from The Ancient of Days (the app's painting for hexagram 1), speaks as pure creative force; the Guide's narrator gives line 6's turn. The user, 2026-09-30: 'the guide shorts are a real format ... let's go ahead and do a short with the Urizen talking head with the line six'. Head: blender/urizen.py (faceted, neon backdrop, no eyeballs). Notes: docs/notes/2026-09-30-metal-treatments.md.

urizen.note: the user's pick, 2026-09-30 ('try this voice id for urizen'); audition of David, Anthony Brownstone and Bill in out/voice/urizen-audition

guide.name: hitchiker's guide v1
guide.note: the user's designed Guide voice ('love it')

narration.text: I am Urizen. I measure everything.
Six solid lines. Heaven never rests. Neither do I.
The dragon rose. The dragon flew. And I keep climbing.
The I Ching. Qián, top line: the dragon that went too high. There is regret.
narration.say: The I Ching. Chyen, top line: the dragon that went too high. There is regret.

narration.text: An old commentary explains: it knows how to advance, not how to withdraw.
William Blake's Urizen makes rules for everything.

narration.direction: baffled disbelief; the sun outline goes out at once

onScreen.label: SUBJECT: URIZEN / OCCUPATION: MEASURING
onScreen.hexagram: Qián 乾 (The Creative): six solid lines, line 6 (the top) lit amber on beat 4
onScreen.quote: 知進而不知退 KNOWS HOW TO ADVANCE, NOT HOW TO WITHDRAW (beat 5)

sources.line6: 上九：亢龍有悔 (Top Nine: the arrogant, over-high dragon has regret).
sources.smallImage: 亢龍有悔，盈不可久也 (what is full cannot last).
sources.wenyan: 亢之為言也，知進而不知退，知存而不知亡，知得而不知喪 (Wenyan, one of the Ten Wings: 'lofty' means knowing to advance but not to withdraw, to keep but not to lose, to gain but not to let go).
sources.wangBi: On line 2: 上則過亢 ('in the top position one is excessively lofty'), 8bitoracle-next/src/constants/wangBiZhu.ts.
sources.qian: Six yang lines; Image: 天行健，君子以自強不息 (heaven moves strongly; the noble one strengthens himself without rest). Lines 1-5: hidden dragon, dragon in the field, ceaselessly active, perhaps leaping, flying dragon in heaven.
sources.blake: Urizen in Blake's mythology is the figure of limiting reason and law; The Ancient of Days (1794) is the frontispiece to Europe: A Prophecy. The app's commentary (sixlines-ios, artwork_treatises_01-08.json) reads the figure as the creative force.

review: Astra (gpt-6.1-sol, high), docs/research/2026-09-30-codex-urizen-qian6.md: change; Opus agreed with every change, so round 1 converged.
